answer: A concrete Sybil defense is VRF-sampled juries: each epoch a verifiable random function draws graders from the established set, weighted by reputation, and their choices stay secret until reveal. A farm cannot predict or target the panel, so extra keys buy no leverage; only a vertex of genuine reputation shifts the odds. The orchard of identities is thus filtered by work already judged, and a pigment of new keys cannot paint over a missing record. Coercion fails too, because no one knows the panel in advance. The attacker must earn reputation across many honest rounds, not mint addresses.
